title: Gambas al Ajillo (Spanish Garlic Shrimp)
short: Shrimp sizzling in garlicky olive oil with smoked paprika. Bring bread for dipping.
keywords: Gambas al Ajillo (Spanish Garlic Shrimp), date night, dinner for two, playful, cozy
intro: In Spanish tapas bars, gambas al ajillo arrives still bubbling in a small clay dish. The flavored oil is half the point: garlic, chili and smoked paprika steeped in good olive oil, soaked up with crusty bread. It works as a starter or, with a salad, a relaxed main.
why: Served straight from the hot pan in the middle of the table, it turns dinner into sharing, which is the point.

ings.h: 300 g (10 oz)
80 ml (⅓ cup)

ings.i: red pepper flakes or 1 small dried chili
crusty bread, to serve (skip for gluten-free)

steps.t: Toss the shrimp with the salt and baking soda and leave for 15 minutes. Pat dry.
Put the oil, garlic and chili in a cold skillet or small cazuela. Set over medium-low heat and cook gently for 3–4 minutes until the garlic is fragrant and pale gold. Do not let it brown.
Turn the heat to medium-high, add the shrimp in one layer and cook for 1 minute. Flip, sprinkle with paprika, add the sherry and cook about 1 minute more until just pink and opaque.
Off the heat, add the lemon juice and parsley. Serve sizzling in the pan with bread for dipping.

tips: Garlic goes from golden to bitter in seconds. Starting it in cold oil gives you control.
Leave the tails on for a prettier plate, or off for easier eating.
makeahead: Peel the shrimp and slice the garlic in the morning; cooking takes six minutes.
plating: Serve it in the pan it was cooked in on a wooden board, with a folded napkin for the handle.
wine: Albariño or a chilled fino sherry.

faq.a: Yes. Thaw in cold water for 10 minutes and dry well before salting.
